newsitem.title: UK: UK TUC says EMU criteria must be flexible.
newsitem.headline: UK TUC says EMU criteria must be flexible.

text.p: John Monks, general secretary of Britain's Trades Union Congress (TUC), said the convergence criteria for taking part in a single European currency should be interpreted flexibly.

Addressing a TUC conference on "Social Europe," he said the union umbrella group believed that if monetary union went ahead with the required number of countries, the balance of advantage lay in Britain joining.
"That said...we are better placed to press our argument about the scope for flexibility in interpreting the convergence criteria," Monks said.

"The criteria are reference values, not precise commandments. We believe that governments are increasingly coming to our view on a flexible interpretation even, paradoxically, when they say they are dead set against any fudge."'
Monks said the TUC was broadly positive towards EMU but recognised that voters had to be convinced that it would bring economic security in its wake.

The European Union had focussed too much on maintaining financial stability and not enough on jobs. "Governments must realise that, to advance on Europe, their citizens will want to see a Europe that can deliver on jobs," Monks added.
